verdict.headline: Oil shock read as inflation, not fear: hike bets rise even as factory data collapses
verdict.label: Chicago PMI contracts to 47.1 while September hike odds reach 66%; energy leads, gold and crypto fall
verdict.rationale_short: Manufacturing activity contracted sharply and rate-hike odds rose in the same session, with oil the link between them. The cross-asset signature — gold down, yields at a 20-month high, dollar slightly lower — shows the market pricing the Iran escalation as an inflation event rather than a risk event, which removes the growth-relief valve equities have leaned on since June. A 30Y close above 5.30% or a payrolls print above 200K would confirm the frame; Brent back under $87 would dissolve it.

supporting_data.label: Chicago PMI 47.1 versus 57.9 consensus, down from 57.6 — weakest print of 2026
September hike odds 66.1% for the Sep 15-16 FOMC, roughly double the pre-Jackson Hole level; PCE 3.7% over 12 months, 4.1% over six
Brent $90.69 (+2.93%) after US-Iran strikes and a tanker mined in the Strait of Hormuz
10Y topped 4.75%, highest since January 2025, as oil lifted rate-hike expectations
Gold fell 1.02% to $4,483.70 — rate expectations overrode the geopolitical haven bid
Energy led sectors with XLE up over 5% in August while rate-sensitive utilities lagged

watchlist_mentions.note: Rose 1.48% to reclaim the $220 structural level and finished August up roughly 7%; a close under $215 breaks the August 26-27 support zone.
Fell 0.89% on Tim Cook's final session as CEO; John Ternus takes over September 1. Transition priced since April, with the September product event the real test.
Slipped to roughly $77,668 as higher rate expectations pressured crypto, giving up the $80K break entirely. The $76,661 support sits 1.3% below.
Only sector with a bid on the session; finished August up more than 5% as Brent cleared $90.

trade_setups.thesis: The long end closed at 5.25%, nearer the 5.30% regime threshold than at any close this cycle, with the oil-inflation input fresh rather than priced. The Bessent buyback program beginning September 9 is the offsetting structural bid.
trade_setups.entry: 5.30% on a daily close marks the threshold crossed; a return under 5.15% says the buyback bid is absorbing supply
trade_setups.invalidation: Brent back under $87 or a soft payrolls print removes the inflation input driving the move
trade_setups.horizon: Next four sessions, through the September 4 jobs report

trade_setups.thesis: Equities have not marked the repricing. The index fell only 0.33% on a session that moved hike odds nine points and oil nearly 3%, and the VIX at 14.92 carries no event premium into a payrolls week.
trade_setups.entry: Holding 7,700 through Wednesday says the rate path is absorbed; losing 7,650 says multiples are adjusting after the fact
trade_setups.invalidation: A reclaim of 7,750 on soft labour data returns the tape to the pre-Jackson Hole frame

trade_setups.thesis: One tanker has been mined in the Strait of Hormuz. The distinction that matters is between headline escalation and measured supply disruption; transit behaviour, not strike counts, is what marks the difference.
trade_setups.entry: Two voluntary transit suspensions by major operators puts $94-100 in play; a CENTCOM pause or Qatari mediation sends it toward $87
trade_setups.invalidation: A confirmed halt in hostilities collapses the risk premium built over the past two sessions
trade_setups.horizon: Days; resolves ahead of or alongside Friday's payrolls

bear_case: The read overstates a single regional data point. The Chicago PMI is a narrow survey that has produced double-digit monthly swings before without the national ISM following, and one session's cross-asset move around a month-end close on light pre-holiday volume is thin evidence for a regime change. Hike odds at 66% reflect Warsh's rhetoric more than incoming data, and a soft ISM and payrolls sequence would unwind them as fast as they were built. If SPX reclaims 7,750 and the 30Y returns below 5.15%, this read no longer holds.
